from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", [
            "Light behaves as a propagating wave.",
            "Waves possess both crests and troughs.",
            "Interference patterns encode crucial information."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Point light source emitting coherent waves
        source = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(source, 'C3')
        
        waves = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 4):
            wave = Circle(radius=0.2 * i, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            wave.move_to(source.get_center())
            waves.add(wave)
        
        self.play(Create(source), FadeIn(waves))
        self.play(
            waves.animate.scale(3).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Waves with crests and troughs
        wave_graph = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(wave_graph, 'B2', 'D5')
        
        self.play(Create(wave_graph))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Interaction with object
        obstacle = Rectangle(height=2, width=0.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(obstacle, 'C5')
        
        # Interference demonstration - simple representation
        interference = VGroup()
        for i in range(-5, 6):
            line = Line(start=np.array([0, i*0.2, 0]), end=np.array([0.5, i*0.2, 0]), color="#00FF00")
            interference.add(line)
        self.place_in_area(interference, 'B4', 'E4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(obstacle), FadeIn(interference))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Physics of Diffraction", [
            "Light bends when encountering obstacles.",
            "Apertures cause waves to spread out.",
            "Shadows form complex interference patterns."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        slit = Line(UP, DOWN, color=GRAY).shift(self.grid["C3"])
        wave = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=PI, color=WHITE)
        
        screen = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GRAY).rotate(PI/2).shift(self.grid["C6"])
        pattern = VGroup(*[Dot(color=PURPLE, radius=0.03).shift(np.array([0, i*0.1, 0])) for i in range(-5, 6)])
        pattern.move_to(self.grid["C6"])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(slit))
        wave_group = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.2 + i*0.2, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=PI, color=WHITE) for i in range(3)])
        wave_group.move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(FadeIn(wave_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        wave_spread = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.5 + i*0.3, start_angle=-PI/1.5, angle=PI/1.5, color="#00FFFF") for i in range(3)])
        wave_spread.move_to(self.grid["C4"])
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wave_group, wave_spread))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(screen), FadeIn(pattern))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Photography captures only light intensity.",
            "Holography also records the phase.",
            "Reference and object beams interfere.",
            "This records a 3D wavefront.",
            "The medium locks this relationship."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Holography: Recording the Wavefront", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        # Reference beam
        ref_beam = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/4)
        # Object beam (scattered)
        obj_beam = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)]).arrange(RIGHT).scale(0.5)
        # Medium / Recording plate
        plate = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=3, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(plate, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(ref_beam, "B2", scale_factor=1)
        self.place_at_grid(obj_beam, "D2", scale_factor=1)
        self.play(Create(ref_beam), Create(obj_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        interference = VGroup(*[Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color="#FF0000").shift(UP*i*0.2) for i in range(-5, 5)])
        self.place_in_area(interference, "B3", "E4", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(interference))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        plate.set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(plate))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Reconstruction: The Diffraction Reversal", [
            "Holograms function as diffraction gratings.",
            "Coherent light illuminates the pattern.",
            "Diffraction reconstructs the original wavefront.",
            "Virtual images appear in 3D.",
            "Wave properties are perfectly restored."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        hologram = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(hologram, 'C3')
        
        reference_beam = VGroup(*[Line(LEFT*3 + UP*i, LEFT*1.5 + UP*i, color=WHITE) for i in np.linspace(-1, 1, 5)])
        
        reconstructed_waves = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=i*0.5, angle=PI/2, arc_center=RIGHT*2, color=YELLOW) for i in range(1, 5)])
        
        virtual_image = Star(n=5, color=TEAL, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(virtual_image, 'C5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(hologram))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(reference_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(reconstructed_waves))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(virtual_image))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Flash(virtual_image))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Principles of Holography and Diffraction: Capturing Light in 3D

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly review the principle of superposition and phase. Visualize light as a wave with crests and troughs, establishing that interference is the foundation for encoding information.
sections.example: Visualizing two ripples in a pond colliding to create a complex interference pattern of peaks and valleys.

sections.title: The Physics of Diffraction
sections.content: Explain how light waves bend and spread around obstacles or through apertures. Introduce the Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction integral conceptually as the way light maps the 'shadow' of an object into a detailed interference pattern.
sections.example: Laser light passing through a tiny pinhole expanding into a circular 'Airy disk' pattern on a screen.

sections.title: Holography: Recording the Wavefront
sections.content: Contrast photography (capturing intensity only) with holography (capturing phase and intensity). Show the 'reference beam' meeting the 'object beam' to lock the phase relationship onto a medium.
sections.example: A futuristic 'Data Cube' device that captures the 3D position of a hummingbird by comparing a direct reference laser pulse with the light scattered off the bird's feathers.

sections.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Reversal
sections.content: Explain that the hologram acts as a complex diffraction grating. When a coherent light source illuminates the hologram, the stored interference pattern diffracts the light to recreate the original wavefront.
sections.example: Using a simple smartphone flashlight behind a piece of holographic film to project a 3D image of a rotating gear into mid-air.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Recap the sequence: Interference (recording) -> Diffraction (reconstruction). Connect this to modern technology such as heads-up displays (HUDs) or secure holographic ID markers.
sections.example: A digital security tag that displays different depth-layered images of a guardian dragon when tilted under a light source.
